seo_title: Cost to Edit a TikTok Video in 2026: Real Rates
h1: How Much Does It Cost to Edit a TikTok Video in 2026?
description: Editing one TikTok video costs $25–75 from a beginner, $75–200 from an experienced freelancer, and $70–80 inside a monthly plan. Here's what moves the price.
lead: Editing a single TikTok video costs $25–75 from a beginner freelancer, $75–200 from an experienced one, and $70–80 per video inside a monthly plan that covers 10 or more videos. Agencies quote $300 and up per clip. The spread comes down to four things: footage quality, turnaround, graphics and how many videos you need each month.
body:
Search for a TikTok editor and you'll see quotes from $20 to $500 for what looks like the same 45-second clip. The range is real, and it isn't random. This guide lays out the 2026 rates for each way of buying TikTok editing, what you get at each tier, and the point where paying per video stops making sense.

TikTok editing rates in 2026, by who does the work

These ranges are compiled from publicly listed freelance marketplace rates, productized studio pricing and agency rate cards as of October 2026.

Who edits itPer TikTok (up to 60 sec)What's typical
Marketplace beginner$20–75Cuts, auto-captions, one revision
Experienced freelancer$75–200Hook editing, custom captions, music, 2–3 revisions
Senior / specialist freelancer$200–500Motion graphics, grading, sound design
Monthly plan (10–40 videos)$70–80Everything included, dedicated editor, 24-hr turnaround
Agency$300–1,500Strategy, account management, team

Hourly pricing exists too — freelance editors charge roughly $25–150 an hour in 2026 — but for short-form work per-video pricing is far more common, because a 45-second TikTok can take anywhere from one to six hours depending on the brief.

What you actually get at each price

$20–75: template editing

Your clip is dropped into a preset. You get trimmed footage, auto-generated captions and possibly a trending sound. No colour grading, no hook engineering, usually a single revision. It's fine for testing whether TikTok is worth your time at all; the inconsistency shows the moment you post three times a week.

$75–200: professional editing

This is where retention-focused editing starts. Expect a deliberate first-three-second hook, pacing cuts every 2–4 seconds, custom animated captions, licensed music and a couple of revision rounds. Rush delivery usually adds 20–40% on top.

$200–500: specialist work

Motion graphics, product call-outs, multi-layer sound design and brand-consistent colour grading. Worth it for a hero piece or a paid campaign; overkill for a daily talking-head clip.

$70–80 per video: monthly plans

Flat fee, dedicated editor, the specialist inclusions built in. At BrandexVideo, for example, 10 videos a month is $799 — $80 per TikTok edit with grading, animated captions, music, thumbnails and unlimited revisions included. At 20 videos it's $1,499 ($75 each) and at 40 videos $2,799 ($70 each). Every video is up to 60 seconds; a longer clip counts as two.

The four things that move the price

  1. Footage quality. Clean phone footage with good light is quick to cut. Shaky, under-lit footage with poor audio adds cleanup time, and editors price that in. Our guide to editing phone videos covers what to send.
  2. Turnaround. Standard is 48–72 hours on marketplaces. 24-hour delivery is the most common surcharge in 2026, typically 20–40%. Monthly plans usually include it.
  3. Graphics and grading. Motion titles, lower thirds, product pop-ups and grading can double or triple a per-video freelance quote. They're the first thing to check when two quotes look very different.
  4. Volume. One video is a project; twenty is an operation. Per-video pricing is efficient up to about five videos a month and inefficient after that.
Ask what counts as one video

Most editors and plans define one video as up to 60 seconds of finished output. A 90-second TikTok is two videos. If a quote doesn't say, ask before you send footage — it's the most common cause of surprise invoices.

Where paying per video stops making sense

Say you post TikToks four times a week — about 16 a month.

OptionMonthly costIncluded
Freelancer at $100 per video$1,600Editing, captions, 2 revisions; grading and rush extra
Freelancer at $150 per video$2,400Editing, captions, music, grading
Monthly plan, 20 videos$1,49920 videos, grading, captions, thumbnails, 24-hr, unlimited revisions

At 16 videos the plan is cheaper than a mid-range freelancer and you still have four videos spare. Below about five videos a month the freelancer wins. Between five and ten it depends on how much the extras matter to you. For the full comparison of buying models, see freelancer vs agency vs subscription.

How to get an accurate quote in one message

Editors quote high when the brief is vague. Send these five things and the number you get back will be the number you pay:

  • Length of raw footage and how it was shot (phone, mirrorless, screen recording)
  • Finished length you want (most TikToks that perform are 21–45 seconds)
  • Caption style, with one example link
  • Turnaround you need
  • How many videos per month, so the editor can price volume

If you'd rather see the work before committing, a small paid test is the cleanest way to compare editors. Our $149 pilot covers three edited videos in three days, with a free 15-second watermarked sample first. faqs.q: How much should I pay to edit a 30-second TikTok?
faqs.a: In 2026, $25–75 from a beginner, $75–200 from an experienced freelancer, or $70–80 per video inside a monthly plan of 10 or more videos. Length under 60 seconds rarely changes the price; the brief and graphics do.

faqs.q: Why is one editor $20 and another $300 for the same TikTok?
faqs.a: The $20 edit is template cutting with auto-captions and one revision. The $300 edit includes hook engineering, custom animated captions, colour grading, motion graphics and sound design. You are paying for the process, not the minutes of footage.

faqs.q: Does rush delivery cost extra for TikTok editing?
faqs.a: Usually yes. 24-hour delivery is the most common surcharge in 2026, typically 20–40% on freelance quotes. Monthly editing plans normally include 24-hour turnaround at no extra cost.

faqs.q: Is a monthly editing plan cheaper than a freelancer?
faqs.a: Once you post more than about five TikToks a month, yes. A $799 plan for 10 videos is $80 per video with grading, captions and unlimited revisions included, which freelancers generally bill as extras.

faqs.q: What counts as one video in TikTok editing pricing?
faqs.a: Most editors and plans define one video as up to 60 seconds of finished output. A 90-second TikTok counts as two videos. Confirm this before sending footage.
